transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
A powerful nor'easter remains stalled off New York and New Jersey, pushing water into
coastal communities.
In Atlantic City, tides reach their highest level since Superstorm Sandy in 2012.
Coastal flood warnings remain in effect today.
NPR's Amy Held reports one storm-related death has been confirmed in New York City.
In Brooklyn, a falling tree killed a worker for the New York Housing Authority, as wind gusts
topped 60 miles per hour.
More than 100,000 power outages were reported from the Mid-Atlantic to New England.
Some New Yorkers kayaked through flooded city streets.
At the Jersey Shore, some areas saw their highest flooding since Superstorm Sandy 14
years ago.
Anne Fitzsimmons, owner of Jay's On Third Restaurant in Stone Harbor, says she and her
team are doing their best to stay afloat.
Everyone is here, all hands on deck, we're going to get cleaned up, we've been getting
rid of the water, we have fans running to dry it out.
Forecasters expect repeated rounds of coastal flooding as the system loops offshore before
moving out early in the week.
Amy Held, NPR News.
Iran says that only diplomacy can end the war with the U.S. and Israel.
That's after President Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and
stop the fighting.
NPR's Kat Lanstorf reports.
In a post on social media, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Iraqchi wrote that Iran was
aware of President Trump's rejection and said that only "negotiated solutions" will end
the conflict now.
He also wrote that Iran is still waiting for an official U.S. response.
Trump told a group of reporters on Saturday that the Iranian plan was not acceptable but
did not give further explanation.
He suggested Iran wanted to make a deal because it's desperate and "losing so badly."
Iran made the proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz at the United Nations General Assembly
in New York last week.
The extended closure of the Strait has caused major disruptions to the world's oil supply.
Kat Lanstorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
A major security incident has been declared in the United Kingdom.
Vicky Barker reports it was close to a British airbase used by U.S. forces.
A number of homes around Fairford Air Base in southwest England have been evacuated,
and British police have arrested several men on suspicion of explosives offenses.
Bomb disposal experts are at the scene, and armed police are reportedly guarding the main
gate of the base.
Fairford has been the scene of protests over the British government's decision this past
summer to allow the U.S. to use it for staging strikes on Iranian missile sites, a decision
which Iran's leadership said at the time made the base a "legitimate target."
For NPR News, I'm Vicky Barker in London.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Tens of thousands of people marched through the streets of Madrid on Saturday, demanding
stronger protections for renters and a ban on evictions when no other housing is available.
The demonstrations followed the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from the apartment where
she had lived for decades.
The building was sold in 2018, and the woman was offered a chance to buy her apartment,
but she couldn't afford it.
Her case has become a symbol of Spain's housing crisis, as rising rents and a shortage of
homes put apartments out of reach for many people.
The competition is fierce during Alaska's annual Fat Bear Week.
People around the world are casting their votes for their favorite bulky brown bear
at Katmai National Park and Preserve.
Alaska Public Media's Ava White has more.
As the brown bears continue fattening up on sockeye salmon, the original field of 16 chunky
competitors is thinning.
Katmai park ranger Sarah Bruce says, "Even if the plum participant you're rooting for
doesn't take the top spot as fat as spare, they're all still winners."
The bears have no idea that this is happening.
They have already won in the fact that they are set to survive another winter hibernation.
Voting in the bracket style competition is closed over the weekend but reopens Monday.
Fat Bear Week ends Tuesday when a chubby champ will be crowned.
You can vote online at fatbearweek.org.
For NPR News, I'm Ava White in Anchorage.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Powerful nor'easter stalls off New York and New Jersey, causing coastal flooding and power outages
Falling tree in Brooklyn kills New York Housing Authority worker during nor'easter wind gusts
Iran says only diplomacy can end war after Trump rejects proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
Major security incident declared near Fairford Air Base in southwest England, several arrests made
Tens of thousands march in Madrid demanding stronger protections for renters and ban on evictions
Katmai National Park holds annual Fat Bear Week competition as brown bears prepare for hibernation
